body:
### Summary

Ctrl+C stops `uv build` and the backend, but the temporary build environment stays in `builds-v0`. `uv cache prune` reports `No unused entries found` and keeps it. The reproduction below leaves one 84 KiB environment.

The backend has no dependencies or child processes. I expect uv to remove its temporary environment after the backend exits.

Related to #18962.

Create a source directory and a separate cache:

```sh
repro_dir=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir "$repro_dir/source"
cat > "$repro_dir/source/pyproject.toml" <<'TOML'
[build-system]
requires = []
build-backend = "backend"
backend-path = ["."]
TOML
cat > "$repro_dir/source/backend.py" <<'PYTHON'
import time

def build_wheel(wheel_directory, config_settings=None, metadata_directory=None):
    print("Build started; press Ctrl+C now", flush=True)
    time.sleep(60)
PYTHON

uv -v --no-config --offline --cache-dir "$repro_dir/cache" build --wheel \
    --python "$(command -v python3.14)" --no-python-downloads \
    "$repro_dir/source" --out-dir "$repro_dir/dist"
```

Press Ctrl+C after the message. Then inspect the cache:

```sh
uv --no-config --cache-dir "$repro_dir/cache" cache prune
find "$repro_dir/cache/builds-v0" -name pyvenv.cfg -print
du -sk "$repro_dir/cache/builds-v0"/.tmp*
```

`pyvenv.cfg` is still present. `du -sk` reports 84 KiB for the temporary directory after prune.

title: uv build leaves a temporary build environment after Ctrl+C
